node_types.name: Store
node_types.definition: A durable per-record persistence node holding the canonical state of a specific concern within tenant_store.

node_types.name: Log
node_types.definition: An append-only ordered history log of events within tenant_store, providing replay and audit semantics.

node_types.name: Router
node_types.definition: A stateful routing/dispatch component that resolves an input to a partition, owner, or downstream sub-node within tenant_store.

node_types.name: Register
node_types.definition: A keyed register of active records with lifecycle (issuance, rotation, destruction) within tenant_store.

node_types.name: Engine
node_types.definition: A stateful resolver/coordinator that maintains derived mappings or identity state within tenant_store.

nodes.definition: Durable per-tenant master record holding the canonical (tenant_id, current plan, current status, current cluster id, residency policy id, home region, current api keys snapshot ref) tuple, single-writer per tenant in the home region, multi-region replicated with bounded lag; the authoritative read for gateway/usage_meter authentication and rate-limit hydration.

Append-only globally-ordered history log of every tombstoned event (key revocation, plan change, cluster suspension, preservation hold, erasure) keyed by (tenant_id, event_kind, hlc, originator_id); tombstones are not subject to last-write-wins and replay drives reconstruction of any sub-store after corruption or restart.

Stateful router that resolves any incoming write or read to its residency partition by consulting the in-force policy_version pinned by region_coordinator; rejects writes whose tenant residency is outside the regions this instance is allowed to host; deny-by-default on stale or missing policy_version.

Versioned per-tenant plan/quota timeline holding the ordered list of (plan_version, effective_from_hlc, originator_id) entries; supports point-in-time queries (what plan was in force at hlc T?) and rebuild from tombstone_history_log replay.

Active preservation-hold register keyed on (tenant_id, data_class, scope, time_range, hold_id) recording each active hold with provenance (issuing authority, hlc, custodial reason); held data is exempt from retention rotation; erasure of overlapping data is denied while a hold intersects.

Committed-erasure tombstone log: durable per-tenant erasure tombstones with their offboarding attestations, an append-only no-resurrection blacklist of offboarded tenant ids, and the aggregated certificate of deletion; cascades destruction signals to dependent registers (audit_encryption_key_register).

Tenant-to-cluster identity resolver: holds (tenant_id -> current cluster_id) mapping with versioned cluster reassignment events; consumes cluster-level flags (suspension, abuse) and republishes per-tenant effective-cluster state to tenant_record_store; cluster reassignment is monotonic-versioned to preclude flap under behavioral-signal noise.

Per-tenant audit-encryption-key lifecycle register holding (tenant_id, key_id, status: ISSUED|ROTATED|DESTROYED, hlc, generation): issuance on tenant onboarding, scheduled rotation, and irreversible destruction-on-erasure (crypto-shred) cascaded from erasure_tombstone_log AFTER any in-flight audit writes drain and BEFORE the per-store erasure attestation is finalized; destruction is itself logged and signed.

requirements.description: tenant_store state is replicated across regions with bounded lag; each region can authenticate and rate-limit using local replicas

Concurrent writes to tenant_store across regions resolve under an explicit, documented conflict-resolution policy (CRDT, partition by tenant home region, or write quorum) so that no key revocation can be un-revoked by a conflicting concurrent write
Key and tenant revocations are stored as tombstones with global ordering so any region auth_cache hydration sees a revocation regardless of replication lag direction

Each tenant has an explicit residency policy that constrains the regions in which their tenant data, traffic, and derived telemetry may live; the system enforces this policy at the edge, in tenant_store partitioning, and in metrics_store / usage_meter sharding

Plan-change events (upgrade, downgrade, suspension) are stored and propagated as globally-ordered tombstones with an effective-from timestamp so any region auth_cache and tenant_store hydration sees a consistent view of which plan is in force at any point in time, regardless of replication lag direction.

The system models a tenant_cluster identity that groups tenants by signup metadata, source-network fingerprints, behavioral signals, and query-pattern similarity. Every tenant carries a current cluster id; cluster assignment evolves as more behavioral signal accrues.

Cluster-level suspensions (driven by abuse signal) are tombstoned and globally ordered like key revocations, propagate to every region auth_cache via the same fast-path, and reject all member tenants new requests with a documented cluster-suspended rejection reason.

tenant_store supports a documented extract for tenant T operation returning only T data, scoped to the residency policy in force, suitable for fulfilling a lawful-access or DSAR request without disclosing other tenants.

Preservation orders are recorded as tombstoned hold records keyed on (tenant, data_class, scope, time_range); held data is exempt from retention rotation. Holds are globally ordered and propagate cross-region. While a hold is in force, erasure of overlapping data is denied with a documented reason.

Tenant erasure requests are durable tombstones that propagate cross-region like revocations. Each store produces a verifiable per-store deletion attestation; the aggregate certificate of deletion is auditable. Erasure-preservation conflicts resolve under a documented preservation-wins policy.

Once a tenant is offboarded and the erasure attestation is final, that tenant identity cannot be resurrected. Restoring service to the same human/organization requires a new tenant identity. Attempts to reuse an offboarded tenant id are rejected with a documented reason.

Per-tenant audit-encryption-keys have an explicit lifecycle (issuance on onboarding, scheduled rotation, irreversible destruction-on-erasure) and key destruction must occur after any in-flight audit writes drain and before per-store erasure attestation is finalized so compliance_audit crypto-shred is enforceable.

satisfactions.explanation: tenant_record_store is the master per-tenant record, multi-region replicated with bounded lag; each region can read locally for gateway/usage_meter authentication.
tenant_record_store is single-writer per tenant in the home region; tombstone_history_log carries globally-ordered revocations as cascades_to into tenant_record_store; cannot un-revoke.
tombstone_history_log is the append-only globally-ordered home for revocations; cascades to tenant_record_store and to tenant_cluster_identity_engine for fast-path propagation.

residency_partition_router resolves every read/write to its residency partition under in-force policy_version; rejects out-of-residency writes; reads from tenant_record_store and plan_version_timeline scoped by residency.

plan_version_timeline holds versioned (plan_version, effective_from_hlc) entries; rebuilt from tombstone_history_log replay; tenant_record_store sees current-plan via writes_to from plan_version_timeline.
tenant_cluster_identity_engine maintains the (tenant_id -> cluster_id) mapping with monotonic-versioned reassignment events and republishes effective-cluster state to tenant_record_store.

tenant_cluster_identity_engine consumes cluster-suspension tombstones cascaded from tombstone_history_log and writes cluster-suspended state to tenant_record_store; auth_cache fast-path consumes the resulting hydration.

residency_partition_router scopes every extract operation to the residency partition; reads tenant_record_store + plan_version_timeline + preservation_hold_register + erasure_tombstone_log scoped by residency to produce a tenant-only view.

preservation_hold_register holds active (tenant, data_class, scope, time_range) entries with provenance; reads_from erasure_tombstone_log so an incoming erasure that intersects an active hold is denied with documented reason.

erasure_tombstone_log is the durable home for erasure tombstones; cascades destruction to tenant_record_store and audit_encryption_key_register; aggregates per-store attestations into the certificate of deletion.
erasure_tombstone_log carries the append-only no-resurrection blacklist of offboarded tenant ids; any attempt to onboard a blacklisted id is rejected with documented reason.

audit_encryption_key_register holds per-tenant key lifecycle (ISSUED|ROTATED|DESTROYED) with destruction cascaded from erasure_tombstone_log strictly ordered after in-flight audit drains and strictly before per-store erasure attestation finalization.
